severityModal.title: Sector Severity
severityModal.intro: Each sector is scored 0-100 using weighted combinations of MSNA survey indicators across three dimensions: disruption to living standards (access, availability, and quality of essential services), coping mechanisms adopted by affected populations, and physical and mental wellbeing outcomes.
severityModal.footnote: Thresholds are prototype-stage and pending validation against JIAF cluster standards and NRC benchmarks.

pinModal.title: People in Need
pinModal.intro: Estimated from the sector severity score using the same weighted composite formula that drives the severity label:
pinModal.population: Population data: WorldPop 2026 constrained estimates. Education applies an 18% child population share since the sector score represents school-age children only.
pinModal.footnote: Education child share will be replaced by WorldPop age-sex breakdown when available.

assessmentModal.title: Assessment Level
assessmentModal.intro: Indicates how the sector assessment was produced and which data sources it draws on.
assessmentModal.level1Description: Sourced from MSNA (Multi-Sector Needs Assessment) survey data, August 2025. District-level coverage only. No AI review has been applied.
assessmentModal.level2Description: An AI model has reviewed available signals and reports alongside the MSNA baseline to produce an updated severity assessment and written sector summary.
assessmentModal.level3Description: A Rapid Needs Assessment conducted in-field provides direct on-the-ground data, superseding remote-sensing and survey estimates.

precisionModal.title: Precision
precisionModal.intro: Indicates the finest geographic granularity at which the assessment data was collected.
precisionModal.districtDescription: Data collected at administrative level 2 (A2 district). This is the current granularity of the MSNA dataset.
precisionModal.localityDescription: Data collected at sub-district (locality) level, providing finer resolution. Requires field validation or higher-resolution data sources not yet integrated.
precisionModal.footnote: Most current assessments are at District level. Locality precision will become available as finer data sources are integrated.

presenceModal.title: Operational Presence
presenceModal.intro: Sourced from OCHA's 3W (Who does What Where) dataset. Shows humanitarian organizations actively operating in the district, broken down by organization type.

informModal.title: INFORM Risk Index: Methodology
informModal.intro: The INFORM Risk Index is produced by the EU Joint Research Centre (JRC) in partnership with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC). It measures the risk of humanitarian crises and disasters that could overwhelm national response capacity. Scores range from 0 to 10 (higher = more risk).
informModal.pillarHazard: Hazard and Exposure: likelihood of physical events (natural hazards, conflict) affecting the population.
informModal.pillarVulnerability: Vulnerability: socio-economic factors that make communities less able to cope, including poverty, inequality, and displacement.
informModal.pillarCoping: Lack of Coping Capacity: institutional and infrastructure capacity to respond - governance, health system, communication.

modal.title: INFORM Severity Index: Methodology
modal.intro: The INFORM Severity Index is a joint product of the EU Joint Research Centre (JRC), ACAPS, and OCHA. JRC owns the methodology; ACAPS collects the data and produces the monthly scores; OCHA coordinates the initiative. As of the February 2026 release (Version 2026 methodology), scores use a continuous scale of 0 to 10, rescaled from the previous 0 to 5 range for consistency with other INFORM products. Scores are grouped into five severity categories. Only countries with an active humanitarian crisis are included.
modal.dimImpact: Impact: scale and depth of humanitarian needs, including people affected, displacement, and mortality.
modal.dimConditions: Conditions of affected people: living standards, food security, health, water and sanitation, and protection environment.
modal.dimComplexity: Complexity: factors constraining response such as conflict intensity, access restrictions, and political instability.
modal.limitationJudgement: Scores reflect ACAPS analytical judgement and may lag 4 to 8 weeks behind rapidly evolving situations.
modal.limitationCoverage: The index covers active humanitarian crises only. Countries without an active crisis are not included.
modal.sourceAcaps: ACAPS INFORM Severity Index (data and API)
modal.sourceNote: Data is fetched from the ACAPS API, which is identical to the JRC-published monthly dataset. The JRC portal may lag by one release; ACAPS and HDX are authoritative for the latest scores. Updated monthly.

modal.title: IDP Displacement: Methodology
modal.intro: This card shows the total number of conflict-induced internally displaced persons (IDPs) tracked by IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) for the selected country. The figure reflects the latest available snapshot, not a cumulative total.
modal.numberCurrent: Current count: most recent IDP figure from IOM DTM for the country.
modal.numberDelta: Month-over-month delta: change in reported IDPs compared to the previous month's data point.
modal.numberTrend: Trend sparkline: historical monthly IDP counts showing displacement trajectory.
modal.numberFreshness: Freshness dot: green if updated within 30 days, amber within 90 days, red if older.
modal.limitationFloods: Flood and disaster displacement is not included. IOM DTM in this context tracks conflict-induced displacement only.
modal.limitationCoverage: Coverage is limited to IOM DTM's monitoring footprint, which may not capture all displacement situations within a country.
modal.limitationLag: Data may lag 4 to 8 weeks behind real-world conditions depending on the country operation.
modal.sourceNote: HAPI aggregates IOM DTM data alongside other humanitarian datasets under OCHA's stewardship.
